read: The defining event since yesterday's run was the FDA's complete response letter for Summit/Akeso's ivonescimab. The agency would not accept a HARMONi PFS win without a statistically significant OS benefit; SMMT closed -16.5% and every PD-1xVEGF programme is now on notice that OS is the currency in narrow settings. The broad market sold off hard on Monday (S&P 500 -1.9%, Nasdaq -2.5%, VIX ~23), but biotech moved on idiosyncratic news: clean registrational data was paid for (CG Oncology +14% on PIVOT-006, Lexeo +11%). Big pharma kept buying differentiated, de-risked assets: J&J paid $2.2bn upfront for Ollin's Vabysmo challenger with Blackstone funding the Phase 3s (the second Blackstone-funded pharma Phase 3 in a week, after Pfizer), and Lilly logged its 14th acquisition of 2026. Regulators were otherwise generous (Roche's giredestrant four weeks early, Gazyva in pMN, AZ's Klygefa), and European capital formation led the private market (Sofinnova's biggest fund, Flagship London, Biogen-TrimTech). Net: selective risk-on for de-risked assets; risk-off for stories leaning on surrogate endpoints or a lenient FDA.

items.headline: Summit Therapeutics / Akeso: FDA rejects ivonescimab (PD-1xVEGF) in EGFRm NSCLC after TKI
items.detail: The CRL says substantial evidence of effectiveness is not established without a statistically significant OS gain; PFS benefit (HR 0.52) alone does not support a positive benefit-risk. SMMT closed -16.5% (~$11.82); Akeso fell as much as 32% in Hong Kong. The read-across is to the whole class (BioNTech/BMS, Merck, Pfizer all have PD-1xVEGF bispecifics) and to Summit's HARMONi-3 vs pembrolizumab, where OS is a dual primary. AstraZeneca is an equity investor in Summit.

items.headline: J&J acquires Ollin Biosciences for $2.2bn upfront; Blackstone funds the OLN324 Phase 3s
items.detail: OLN324 is a VEGF x Ang-2 bispecific, the same targets as Roche's Vabysmo; a Phase 1b head-to-head suggested faster and larger improvements than Vabysmo. Blackstone Life Sciences commits $750m to fully fund Phase 3 (nAMD trials use Lucentis and Eylea as comparators). This is a direct threat to Roche's ophthalmology franchise and Regeneron's Eylea, and a second pharma Phase 3 funded off-balance-sheet by Blackstone in a week.

items.headline: CG Oncology: PIVOT-006 Phase 3 positive for cretostimogene in intermediate-risk/HG Ta NMIBC
items.detail: Recurrence risk was cut 68% vs surveillance (HR 0.32, 95% CI 0.23-0.45, p<0.0001; n=367; median follow-up 17 months), with no grade >=3 TRAEs or treatment-related discontinuations. CGON closed +14% (~$7.5bn market cap). BLA in BCG-unresponsive disease by March 2027 and an IR-NMIBC filing in Q2 2027 broaden the label into a ~50,000-patient adjuvant population with no approved option. It also competes with J&J's Inlexzo in high-risk disease. Data at SUO on 2 December.

items.headline: Lilly buys stealth biotech Calytrix Bio for up to $1.5bn: its 14th acquisition of 2026
items.detail: The deal adds a preclinical mutant-CALR antibody for essential thrombocythaemia and myelofibrosis. The upfront is not disclosed in the accessible text. It is an early-stage, biobuck-heavy deal, but another sign that Lilly is using GLP-1 cash to build haematology and immunology optionality.

items.headline: Roche: FDA approves giredestrant (Wilserdly) plus everolimus in ER+/HER2- ESR1-mutated advanced breast cancer
items.detail: Approval came about four weeks ahead of the goal date, based on evERA (n=373, 207 ESR1m; investigator-assessed PFS primary). It is Roche's first oral SERD on the market, entering a niche alongside Lilly's Inluriyo and Menarini's Orserdu; the bigger value test is the adjuvant setting.

items.headline: Roche: Gazyva becomes the first FDA-approved therapy for primary membranous nephropathy
items.detail: FDA approved it on 13 November and Roche announced on 16 November. MAJESTY showed 36.1% vs 5.7% complete remission of proteinuria at two years vs tacrolimus. This is Gazyva's third immune-kidney approval (after LN and INS), extending its life-cycle well beyond haem-onc.

items.headline: AstraZeneca (Alexion): Klygefa (gefurulimab) approved in the US for AChR+ gMG, the first once-weekly self-administered SC C5 inhibitor
items.detail: PREVAIL Phase 3 showed MG-ADL -1.6 vs placebo at week 26, with benefit sustained to one year. The EU nod is also in hand per Fierce. It defends Alexion's complement franchise against FcRn competition (argenx's Vyvgart, J&J's Imaavy).

items.headline: Helus Pharma: first psilocybin-class Phase 3 win in adjunctive MDD (HLP003, APPROACH)
items.detail: MADRS fell 19.5 vs 11.9 points at week 6 (-7.6, p<0.0001), with -7.0 sustained at week 12 and remission of 50.9% vs 18.2% (n=222). There were three treatment-related SAEs, which is the debate. The second pivotal, EMBRACE, reads out in Q4 2027, with an NDA targeted for 2028. It supports the psychedelic thesis behind Lilly's AtaiBeckley buy.

items.headline: Seawolf Therapeutics launches with $100m and a Sanofi pact worth up to $1.2bn for redosable LNP-DNA medicines
items.detail: The raise combines a seed led by Versant with a Series A (Versant, MPM BioImpact, Novartis Venture Fund; Lilly and CRISPR Therapeutics participating). The Sanofi deal carries an undisclosed upfront, milestones and royalties, with bleeding disorders first. Tiered as Tier 2 because the $1.2bn is almost all milestones. It is a non-viral, redosable alternative to AAV; the lead programme (muscle/fat) is still in animals.

items.headline: Biogen signs a $411m option deal with Cambridge (UK) degrader biotech TrimTech
items.detail: Terms are up to $32m upfront plus research milestones, with TRIM21-based TRIMTAC/TRIMGLUE degraders aimed at toxic aggregates in neurodegeneration. Biogen holds an option on a global exclusive licence. It is a cheap entry into aggregate-selective degradation.

items.headline: Lexeo: LX2020 (PKP2 ACM gene therapy) interim data; FDA open to NSVT as a surrogate for accelerated approval
items.detail: The high-dose cohorts showed an 80% mean NSVT reduction and 44% fewer PVCs (10 dosed, 9 with >=12 months). LXEO rose ~11%. A regulatory path via a surrogate is the real news for cardiac gene therapy.

items.headline: Aclaris: bosakitug (anti-TSLP) fails Phase 2 ADMIRATION in atopic dermatitis; programme dropped
items.detail: It missed EASI at week 24 and the secondaries (n=110) despite target engagement. ACRS fell 6.6%. Another TSLP-in-AD miss after Sanofi's in April.

items.headline: Flagship commits £100m to an AI-focused company-creation lab in London
items.detail: It is Flagship's first venture-creation unit outside Cambridge, MA, starting with ~50 scientist-entrepreneurs. It is a vote for UK talent despite pharma's UK investment freeze.

items.headline: Windward Bio closes its IPO at $251.2m gross (update)
items.detail: The underwriters exercised the greenshoe in full and Sanofi's $50m placement closed. Shares rose ~68% on the 13 November debut. New since Friday: the deal closed and the size grew.

items.headline: Commit Biologics completes a $60m seed for complement-powered immune engagers
items.detail: Ackermans & van Haaren led the round, with AbbVie Ventures and M Ventures joining Novo Holdings and others. COM002 is heading to the clinic.

items.headline: Biocon wins FDA approval for Pebrilzo, a Perjeta (pertuzumab) biosimilar
items.detail: The Genentech settlement sets Q3 2028 as the earliest US launch, so Roche has no near-term impact.

items.headline: China fires two researchers after a child's death in a gene-editing study
items.detail: The probe found an unreported preclinical safety signal, an inadequate consent form, undisclosed conflicts and ~$160k in gifts from families. Expect tighter Chinese CGT trial oversight.
